questions.question: The price of a phone is increased by 20% and the new price is then decreased by 20%. What is the net change in price?
questions.solution: Net change = a + b + ab/100 = 20 − 20 − (20×20)/100 = −4%, i.e. a 4% decrease.

questions.question: A's salary is 25% more than B's. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?
questions.solution: Let B = 100, so A = 125. B is less than A by 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

questions.question: If 40% of a number is 96, what is 65% of the same number?
A town's population is 50,000. It grows by 10% in the first year and 20% in the second. What is the population after 2 years?
A student scoring 30% fails by 30 marks. Another student scoring 45% gets 15 marks more than the pass mark. What are the maximum marks?
The price of sugar rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its spending on sugar stays the same?
An article bought for ₹800 is sold for ₹1,000. What is the profit percentage?
An item has a marked price of ₹1,200 and is sold at a 15% discount. What is the selling price?
A shopkeeper marks goods 40% above cost price and gives a 10% discount. What is his profit percentage?
Selling an item for ₹1,140 causes a loss of 5%. At what price should it be sold to make a 5% profit?
Two items are each sold for ₹990, one at a 10% profit and the other at a 10% loss. What is the overall result?
A dishonest dealer sells at cost price but uses a 900 g weight in place of 1 kg. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: He gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g. Profit % = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9%.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
What is the compound interest on ₹10,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually?
What is the difference between compound and simple interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum?
A sum of money doubles in 8 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution: Interest = P in 8 years, so R = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.question: A sum becomes ₹8,820 in 2 years at 5% per annum compound interest. What is the principal?
₹1,800 is divided in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest share?
questions.solution: Total parts = 9, so one part = ₹200. Largest share = 4 × 200 = ₹800.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.solution: Make B equal: A:B = 8:12 and B:C = 12:15, so A:B:C = 8:12:15.

questions.question: A and B invest ₹30,000 and ₹45,000 respectively for one year. The profit is ₹15,000. What is A's share?
What is the mean proportional between 9 and 16?
questions.solution: Mean proportional = √(9 × 16) = √144 = 12.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7 : 5. When 12 more girls join, the ratio becomes 1 : 1. How many boys are there?
The average of 5 numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the average of the rest is 18. What number was removed?
questions.solution: Sum of 5 = 100. Sum of 4 = 72. Removed = 100 − 72 = 28.

questions.question: What is the average of the first 10 natural numbers?
The average age of 30 students is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average becomes 15 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.solution: Sum of 30 ages = 420. Sum of 31 ages = 31 × 15 = 465. Teacher = 465 − 420 = 45 years.

questions.question: In what ratio must rice at ₹40/kg be mixed with rice at ₹55/kg to get a mixture worth ₹45/kg?
questions.solution: Alligation: (55 − 45) : (45 − 40) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1 (cheaper : dearer).

questions.question: A 20-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2?
questions.solution: Milk = 15 L, water = 5 L. For 3 : 2, water must be 10 L, so add 5 L.

questions.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, how long will they take?
questions.solution: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day. Time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.question: 6 men can finish a piece of work in 10 days. How many days will 15 men take?
questions.solution: Total work = 6 × 10 = 60 man-days. 60/15 = 4 days.

questions.question: A and B together can do a job in 10 days. A alone can do it in 15 days. How long will B take alone?
questions.solution: B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so B takes 30 days.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours and pipe B empties it in 9 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?
questions.solution: Net rate = 1/6 − 1/9 = 1/18 per hour, so 18 hours.

questions.question: A can do a job in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, then A leaves. In how many more days will B finish the job?
questions.solution: In 6 days they do 6 × (1/20 + 1/30) = 1/2 of the job. B does the other 1/2 in 30 × 1/2 = 15 days.

questions.question: A 150 m long train runs at 54 km/h. How long does it take to cross a pole?
A car goes from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the round trip?
questions.solution: For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 60 × 40/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.question: A 200 m long train running at 72 km/h crosses a 300 m long platform. How long does it take?
A boat's speed in still water is 15 km/h and the stream flows at 3 km/h. How long does the boat take to go 36 km downstream?
questions.solution: Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Time = 36/18 = 2 h.

questions.question: Two trains, 120 m and 180 m long, run in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other completely?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance = 300 m. Time = 300/25 = 12 s.

questions.question: How many trailing zeros does 50! have?
questions.solution: Count the factors of 5: ⌊50/5⌋ + ⌊50/25⌋ = 10 + 2 = 12.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2¹⁰ is divided by 7?
What is the HCF of 36 and 84?
What is the LCM of 12, 18 and 30?
How many positive factors does 360 have?
What is the unit digit of 7⁹⁵?
questions.solution: Unit digits of powers of 7 repeat 7, 9, 3, 1. 95 mod 4 = 3, so the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, which is 3.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is x² + 1/x²?
If 3x − 7 = 2x + 5, what is x?
If the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0 are a and b, what is a² + b²?
questions.solution: a + b = 5 and ab = 6. a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 25 − 12 = 13. (The roots are 2 and 3.)

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 25 and their difference is 7. What is their product?
questions.solution: The numbers are (25 + 7)/2 = 16 and (25 − 7)/2 = 9. Product = 144.

questions.question: If a + b = 7 and ab = 10, what is a³ + b³?
A right triangle has legs of 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the area of its circumcircle?
questions.solution: Hypotenuse = √(36 + 64) = 10 cm. The hypotenuse is the circumdiameter, so r = 5 and area = 25π cm².

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 12 cm long and 8 cm wide?
questions.solution: Perimeter = 2(l + b) = 2(12 + 8) = 40 cm.

questions.question: What is each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.solution: Each interior angle = (n − 2) × 180°/n = 4 × 180/6 = 120°.

questions.question: A cube has a total surface area of 150 cm². What is its volume?
questions.solution: 6a² = 150 ⇒ a = 5 cm. Volume = 5³ = 125 cm³.

questions.question: What is the area of an equilateral triangle with side 6 cm?
If the radius of a circle increases by 10%, by what percentage does its area increase?
questions.solution: Area ∝ r². 1.1² = 1.21, so the area increases by 21%.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word LEVEL be arranged?
questions.solution: 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5!/(2! × 2!) = 30.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 people sit in a row?
In how many ways can a committee of 3 be chosen from 8 people?
How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
A committee of 3 is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. In how many ways can this be done if it must include at least one woman?
questions.solution: Total = 9C3 = 84. All-men = 5C3 = 10. At least one woman = 84 − 10 = 74.

questions.question: How many diagonals does a regular decagon (10 sides) have?
Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
A card is drawn at random from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability that it is a king?
questions.solution: There are 4 kings: 4/52 = 1/13.

questions.question: Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least two heads?
questions.solution: Outcomes with 2 or 3 heads: HHT, HTH, THH, HHH, which is 4 of 8, so 1/2.

questions.question: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the product of the numbers is even?
questions.solution: The product is odd only when both are odd: 3 × 3 = 9 outcomes. P(even) = 1 − 9/36 = 3/4.

questions.question: The price of an article is reduced by 15% and then by a further 20%. What is the overall reduction?
questions.solution: Price after both cuts = 0.85 × 0.80 = 0.68 of the original, so the overall reduction is 32%.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates the winner got 55% of the votes cast and won by 1,200 votes. How many votes were cast in all?
questions.solution: The winner got 55% and the loser 45%, a margin of 10% of the votes. 10% of the total = 1,200, so the total = 12,000.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row if two particular people must sit together?
questions.solution: Treat the two people as one block. 4 units can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways, and the two can swap inside the block in 2 ways. Total = 24 × 2 = 48.

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article 20% above its cost price and then allows a discount of 10%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution: Take cost = 100. Marked price = 120. Selling price = 120 × 0.90 = 108. Profit = 8%.

questions.question: A trader sells two articles at ₹1,200 each. On one he gains 20% and on the other he loses 20%. What is his overall result?
questions.solution: The first cost 1,200/1.2 = ₹1,000. The second cost 1,200/0.8 = ₹1,500. Total cost = ₹2,500 and total sale = ₹2,400, a loss of ₹100, which is 4% of 2,500.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 3 years?
What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹10,000 for 2 years at 10% per annum?
questions.solution: For 2 years the difference = P × (R/100)² = 10,000 × (0.1)² = ₹100.

questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself?
questions.solution: Doubling in 5 years means the interest in 5 years equals the principal, so the interest per year is P/5. To reach 4P the interest must be 3P, which takes 3 × 5 = 15 years.

questions.question: If A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 6 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.solution: Make B equal in both ratios. A : B = 3 : 4 = 9 : 12 and B : C = 6 : 5 = 12 : 10. So A : B : C = 9 : 12 : 10.

questions.question: The average of five numbers is 24. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining four becomes 22. What is the number removed?
questions.solution: Sum of five = 5 × 24 = 120. Sum of four = 4 × 22 = 88. The removed number = 120 − 88 = 32.

questions.question: In what ratio should rice costing ₹40 per kg be mixed with rice costing ₹60 per kg to get a mixture worth ₹48 per kg?
questions.solution: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (60 − 48) : (48 − 40) = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.

questions.question: A can complete a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.solution: Together they do 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the job per day, so they take 6 days.

questions.question: A and B together can finish a job in 12 days. A alone can finish it in 20 days. In how many days can B alone finish it?
questions.solution: B's daily work = 1/12 − 1/20 = 5/60 − 3/60 = 2/60 = 1/30, so B alone takes 30 days.

questions.question: A train 150 m long passes a pole in 10 seconds. What is its speed?
questions.solution: Speed = 150/10 = 15 m/s. In km/h that is 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.question: A man goes 60 km at 30 km/h and returns the same 60 km at 20 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole trip?
questions.solution: Total distance = 120 km. Time = 60/30 + 60/20 = 2 + 3 = 5 hours. Average speed = 120/5 = 24 km/h.

questions.question: Two trains of length 120 m and 180 m run in opposite directions at 54 km/h and 36 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 54 + 36 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance to cover = 120 + 180 = 300 m. Time = 300/25 = 12 s.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2^50 is divided by 7?
questions.solution: Powers of 2 repeat their remainders modulo 7 in a cycle of 3: 2, 4, 1. Since 50 = 3 × 16 + 2, the remainder is the 2nd in the cycle, which is 4.

questions.question: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.solution: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, so x² + 1/x² = 23.

questions.question: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. What is its area? (Take π = 22/7)
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.solution: Favourable = 4C2 = 6. Total = 10C2 = 45. Probability = 6/45 = 2/15.

questions.question: What is 35% of 240?
A number is increased by 30% and the result is then decreased by 10%. What is the net percentage change?
questions.solution: Take the number as 100. After +30%: 130. After −10% of 130: 130 − 13 = 117. The net change is a 17% increase.

questions.question: A's income is 20% more than B's. By what percentage is B's income less than A's?
questions.solution: Let B = 100, so A = 120. B is less than A by 20/120 = 16.67%.

questions.question: In an exam 40% of the candidates failed. If 300 candidates passed, how many appeared?
questions.solution: The pass percentage is 60%. 60% of the candidates = 300, so the total = 300/0.60 = 500.

questions.question: The population of a town grows by 10% every year. Its present population is 21,780. What was it two years ago?
An article bought for ₹480 is sold for ₹552. What is the profit percentage?
A shopkeeper gives a discount of 12% on the marked price and still gains 10%. If the cost price is ₹800, what is the marked price?
questions.solution: Selling price = 800 × 1.10 = ₹880. This is 88% of the marked price, so the marked price = 880/0.88 = ₹1,000.

questions.question: By selling an article for ₹720 a man loses 10%. At what price should he sell it to gain 10%?
questions.solution: 720 is 90% of the cost, so cost = 720/0.9 = ₹800. For a 10% gain, selling price = 800 × 1.1 = ₹880.

questions.question: A sells an article to B at a 20% profit, and B sells it to C at a 25% profit. If C pays ₹1,500, what did it cost A?
questions.solution: C's price = A's cost × 1.20 × 1.25 = 1.5 × A's cost. So A's cost = 1,500/1.5 = ₹1,000.

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equal to a single discount of:
questions.solution: Price after both = 0.80 × 0.90 = 0.72 of the marked price, so the single discount is 28%.

questions.question: ₹2,000 becomes ₹2,480 in 3 years at simple interest. What is the rate per annum?
What is the compound interest on ₹5,000 at 8% per annum for 2 years?
A sum becomes ₹7,986 in 3 years at 10% per annum compound interest. What is the sum?
A sum lent at simple interest amounts to ₹1,200 in 2 years and ₹1,350 in 5 years. What is the sum?
questions.solution: Interest for 3 years (years 2 to 5) = 1,350 − 1,200 = ₹150, so ₹50 a year. Interest for 2 years = ₹100, so the sum = 1,200 − 100 = ₹1,100.

questions.question: ₹2,400 is divided between A and B in the ratio 5 : 3. How much does A get?
Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 10 is added to each, the ratio becomes 5 : 7. What is the smaller number?
questions.solution: Let the numbers be 3x and 5x. (3x + 10)/(5x + 10) = 5/7 gives 21x + 70 = 25x + 50, so x = 5. The smaller number = 15.

questions.question: A 50-litre mixture has milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. How much water must be added to make the ratio 2 : 1?
questions.solution: Milk = 40 L and water = 10 L. For a 2 : 1 ratio the water must be 20 L, so add 10 L.

questions.question: What is the average of 11, 15, 19, 23 and 27?
questions.solution: The numbers are evenly spaced, so the average is the middle number, 19. Check: 95/5 = 19.

questions.question: The average weight of 20 students is 52 kg. When a new student joins, the average becomes 53 kg. What is the weight of the new student?
questions.solution: New total = 21 × 53 = 1,113 kg. Old total = 20 × 52 = 1,040 kg. The new student weighs 1,113 − 1,040 = 73 kg.

questions.question: Sugar costing ₹30 per kg is mixed with sugar costing ₹45 per kg in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the cost per kg of the mixture?
12 men can complete a work in 20 days. In how many days will 8 men complete it?
questions.solution: Total work = 12 × 20 = 240 man-days. With 8 men, time = 240/8 = 30 days.

questions.question: A, B and C can do a job alone in 10, 12 and 15 days respectively. In how many days will they finish it working together?
questions.solution: Work per day = 1/10 + 1/12 + 1/15 = (6 + 5 + 4)/60 = 15/60 = 1/4. They finish in 4 days.

questions.question: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B fills it in 15 hours. Pipe C empties it in 20 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will the empty tank take to fill?
A car travelling at 45 km/h covers a distance of 270 km. How long does it take?
questions.solution: Time = distance/speed = 270/45 = 6 hours.

questions.question: A boat's speed in still water is 10 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How long does it take to go 24 km downstream and return 24 km upstream?
questions.solution: Downstream speed = 12 km/h, so 24/12 = 2 hours. Upstream speed = 8 km/h, so 24/8 = 3 hours. Total = 5 hours.

questions.question: A walks at 5 km/h. Two hours later B starts from the same point in the same direction at 7 km/h. How many hours after B starts will B catch A?
questions.solution: A has a head start of 5 × 2 = 10 km. B gains 7 − 5 = 2 km every hour, so B catches A in 10/2 = 5 hours.

questions.question: A train crosses a 200 m platform in 25 seconds and a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution: Let the length be L and the speed v. v = L/15 and v = (L + 200)/25. So 25L = 15L + 3,000, which gives L = 300 m.

questions.question: What is the greatest number that divides 1,657 and 2,037 leaving remainders 6 and 5 respectively?
questions.solution: The number divides 1,657 − 6 = 1,651 and 2,037 − 5 = 2,032. 1,651 = 13 × 127 and 2,032 = 16 × 127, so the HCF is 127 (which is larger than both remainders).

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 8^35?
questions.solution: The unit digits of powers of 8 repeat in a cycle of 4: 8, 4, 2, 6. Since 35 = 4 × 8 + 3, the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, 2.

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 24 and their product is 143. What is their difference?
questions.solution: (a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab = 576 − 572 = 4, so the difference is 2. (The numbers are 13 and 11.)

questions.question: If the roots of x² − 9x + 14 = 0 are a and b, what is a² + b²?
questions.solution: a + b = 9 and ab = 14. a² + b² = (a + b)² − 2ab = 81 − 28 = 53.

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm?
questions.solution: Semi-perimeter = 21. Area = √(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7,056 = 84 cm².

questions.question: The total surface area of a cube is 150 cm². What is its volume?
questions.solution: 6a² = 150 gives a² = 25, so a = 5 cm. Volume = 5³ = 125 cm³.

questions.question: What is the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 10 = 440 cm².

questions.question: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 if no digit is repeated?
questions.solution: Choose and arrange 3 of the 5 digits: 5 × 4 × 3 = 60.

questions.question: A committee of 3 is to be chosen from 5 men and 4 women, with at least one woman. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: All committees: 9C3 = 84. Committees with no woman: 5C3 = 10. With at least one woman: 84 − 10 = 74.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word BANANA be arranged?
questions.solution: BANANA has 6 letters with A three times and N twice. Arrangements = 6!/(3! × 2!) = 720/12 = 60.

questions.question: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a king or a queen?
questions.solution: There are 4 kings and 4 queens, so 8 favourable cards. Probability = 8/52 = 2/13.

questions.question: Two fair coins and one fair die are thrown together. What is the probability of getting two heads and an even number?
questions.solution: P(two heads) = 1/4 and P(even number) = 1/2. They are independent, so the probability = 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8.

questions.question: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is a multiple of 5?
questions.solution: Sum 5: 4 ways (1,4), (2,3), (3,2), (4,1). Sum 10: 3 ways (4,6), (5,5), (6,4). Favourable = 7 out of 36, so the probability = 7/36.

questions.question: A company's headcount rises from 800 to 920. What is the percentage increase?
questions.solution: Increase = 920 − 800 = 120. Percentage increase = 120/800 × 100 = 15%.

questions.question: In a campus drive, 25% of 640 students were shortlisted and 40% of the shortlisted students received offers. How many students received offers?
questions.solution: Shortlisted = 25% of 640 = 160. Offers = 40% of 160 = 64.

questions.question: A package of ₹6 lakh is raised by 20% and then cut by 20%. What is the final package?
questions.solution: After the raise: 6 × 1.2 = 7.2. After the cut: 7.2 × 0.8 = ₹5.76 lakh.

questions.question: A laptop bought for ₹40,000 is sold at a 15% profit. What is the selling price?
An item is marked at ₹1,250 and sold after a 20% discount, still giving a 25% profit. What is the cost price?
An item costs ₹500 and is marked 40% above cost. After a 15% discount, what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Marked price = 500 × 1.4 = ₹700. Selling price = 700 × 0.85 = ₹595. Profit = 95, which is 95/500 = 19%.

questions.question: What is the simple interest on ₹12,000 at 7.5% per annum for 4 years?
At what rate of simple interest per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years?
questions.solution: The interest equals the principal: P = P × r × 8/100, so r = 100/8 = 12.5%.

questions.question: Two employees' salaries are in the ratio 5 : 7 and together amount to ₹60,000. What is the difference between them?
questions.solution: One part = 60,000/12 = ₹5,000. The salaries are ₹25,000 and ₹35,000, a difference of ₹10,000.

questions.question: Among 240 candidates the ratio of boys to girls is 7 : 5. If 20 more girls join, what is the new ratio of boys to girls?
questions.solution: Boys = 140 and girls = 100. After 20 more girls: 140 : 120 = 7 : 6.

questions.question: The average of six consecutive even numbers is 15. What is the largest of them?
questions.solution: For consecutive even numbers the average is the middle of the list: the 3rd and 4th numbers are 14 and 16. So the numbers are 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 and the largest is 20.

questions.question: Thirty students have an average score of 60 and twenty students have an average of 70. What is the average of all fifty students?
In what ratio should a 20% salt solution be mixed with a 50% salt solution to get a 30% solution?
questions.solution: Using alligation: (50 − 30) : (30 − 20) = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1, the 20% solution to the 50% solution.

questions.question: A can finish a task in 12 days and B can finish it in 24 days. How long will they take working together?
questions.solution: Work per day = 1/12 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8. They finish in 8 days.

questions.question: 8 workers can finish a job in 15 days. After 5 days, 8 more workers join. How many more days will it take to finish the job?
questions.solution: Total work = 8 × 15 = 120 worker-days. In 5 days 40 are done, leaving 80. With 16 workers the rest takes 80/16 = 5 days.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 8 hours and pipe B in 12 hours. Both are opened for 3 hours and then B is closed. How many more hours will A take to fill the rest?
questions.solution: In 3 hours both fill 3 × (1/8 + 1/12) = 3 × 5/24 = 5/8 of the tank. The remaining 3/8 is filled by A alone in 3/8 × 8 = 3 hours.

questions.question: A car travels 120 km at 60 km/h and returns the same 120 km at 40 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole trip?
questions.solution: Time going = 2 h and time returning = 3 h. Average speed = 240/5 = 48 km/h.

questions.question: A 150 m long train running at 54 km/h passes a pole. How long does it take?
Two trains of lengths 100 m and 125 m run in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. How long do they take to cross each other?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Distance = 225 m. Time = 225/25 = 9 seconds.

questions.question: A boat goes upstream at 12 km/h and downstream at 20 km/h. What is its speed in still water?
questions.solution: Speed in still water = (20 + 12)/2 = 16 km/h.

questions.question: What is the smallest number which leaves a remainder of 5 when divided by 6, 8 and 12?
questions.solution: LCM of 6, 8 and 12 = 24. The smallest such number is 24 + 5 = 29.

questions.question: What is the sum of all multiples of 7 from 1 to 100?
If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is the value of a² + b²?
The product of two consecutive positive integers is 342. What is their sum?
questions.solution: 18 × 19 = 342, so the integers are 18 and 19 and their sum is 37.

questions.question: The perimeter of a rectangle is 36 cm and its length is twice its breadth. What is its area?
questions.solution: 2(l + b) = 36 with l = 2b gives 6b = 36, so b = 6 and l = 12. Area = 72 cm².

questions.question: The area of a circle is 154 cm². What is its circumference? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution: πr² = 154 gives r² = 49, so r = 7. Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 7 = 44 cm.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word CAMPUS be arranged so that the two vowels are together?
questions.solution: Treat the vowels A and U as one block. The 5 units (C, M, P, S and the block) can be arranged in 5! = 120 ways, and the vowels in the block can swap in 2 ways. Total = 240.

questions.question: In how many ways can a team of 4 be chosen from 10 candidates?
A bag has 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is not blue?
questions.solution: Not blue = 5 + 2 = 7 balls out of 10. Probability = 7/10.

questions.question: A committee of 2 is chosen at random from 4 men and 3 women. What is the probability that both are women?
questions.solution: Total ways = 7C2 = 21. Both women: 3C2 = 3. Probability = 3/21 = 1/7.

questions.question: If 2x + 3y = 12 and 3x − y = 7, what is the value of x + y?
questions.solution: From the second equation, y = 3x − 7. Substituting in the first: 2x + 9x − 21 = 12, so 11x = 33 and x = 3. Then y = 9 − 7 = 2, and x + y = 5.

questions.question: If x − 1/x = 3, what is the value of x³ − 1/x³?
If a + b + c = 12 and a² + b² + c² = 50, what is the value of ab + bc + ca?
questions.solution: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca). So 144 = 50 + 2(ab + bc + ca), giving ab + bc + ca = 94/2 = 47.

questions.question: If x = 2 + √3, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
Which quadratic equation has roots 3 and −5?
questions.solution: Sum of roots = 3 + (−5) = −2 and product = 3 × (−5) = −15. The equation is x² − (sum)x + product = 0, i.e. x² + 2x − 15 = 0.

questions.question: If a = 13, b = −7 and c = −6, what is the value of a³ + b³ + c³?
questions.solution: Here a + b + c = 13 − 7 − 6 = 0, and whenever a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc. So the value is 3 × 13 × (−7) × (−6) = 1638. (Directly: 2197 − 343 − 216 = 1638.)

questions.question: For what value of k does the equation kx² − 12x + 9 = 0 have two equal roots?
questions.solution: Equal roots need the discriminant to be zero: (−12)² − 4 × k × 9 = 0, i.e. 144 − 36k = 0, so k = 4.

questions.question: 3 pens and 2 notebooks cost ₹110, while 2 pens and 3 notebooks cost ₹115. What is the cost of one pen and one notebook together?
questions.solution: Adding the two equations: 5 pens + 5 notebooks = ₹225, so 1 pen + 1 notebook = ₹45. (Separately, a pen costs ₹20 and a notebook ₹25.)

questions.question: If 4ˣ = 8⁽ˣ⁻¹⁾, what is the value of x?
questions.solution: Write both sides as powers of 2: 4ˣ = 2²ˣ and 8⁽ˣ⁻¹⁾ = 2³ˣ⁻³. So 2x = 3x − 3, giving x = 3.

questions.question: If x² − 6x + 1 = 0, what is the value of x⁴ + 1/x⁴?
questions.solution: Divide x² − 6x + 1 = 0 by x: x + 1/x = 6. Then x² + 1/x² = 6² − 2 = 34, and x⁴ + 1/x⁴ = 34² − 2 = 1156 − 2 = 1154.

questions.question: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first six results is 49 and that of the last six is 52. What is the sixth result?
questions.solution: The sixth result is counted in both groups of six. So it equals (sum of first six) + (sum of last six) − (sum of all eleven) = 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 − 11 × 50 = 294 + 312 − 550 = 56.

questions.question: A vessel contains 40 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are taken out and replaced with water, and the process is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.solution: Each replacement keeps (40 − 8)/40 = 4/5 of the milk. After two operations, milk = 40 × (4/5)² = 40 × 16/25 = 25.6 litres.

questions.question: The average age of a family of 5 members is 30 years. The youngest member is 6 years old. What was the average age of the family just before the youngest member was born?
questions.solution: Total age now = 5 × 30 = 150 years. The other four members total 150 − 6 = 144 years now; 6 years ago they totalled 144 − 4 × 6 = 120 years. Average then = 120/4 = 30 years.

questions.question: What is the average of the first 15 odd natural numbers?
questions.solution: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n², so the sum of the first 15 is 225. Average = 225/15 = 15.

questions.question: A batsman has an average of 40 runs after 20 innings. How many runs must he score in his 21st innings to raise his average to 42?
questions.solution: Runs so far = 20 × 40 = 800. To average 42 after 21 innings he needs 21 × 42 = 882 runs. So he must score 882 − 800 = 82.

questions.question: Milk costs a milkman ₹60 per litre. In what ratio must he mix water with milk so that by selling the mixture at ₹66 per litre he makes a profit of 32%?
questions.solution: Cost price of the mixture = 66/1.32 = ₹50 per litre. Water costs nothing, so by alligation water : milk = (60 − 50) : (50 − 0) = 10 : 50 = 1 : 5.

questions.question: Two alloys contain gold and copper in the ratios 2 : 3 and 3 : 7 respectively. Equal weights of the two alloys are melted together. What is the ratio of gold to copper in the new alloy?
questions.solution: Take 1 kg of each. Gold = 2/5 + 3/10 = 7/10 kg; copper = 3/5 + 7/10 = 13/10 kg. Ratio = 7 : 13.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. What is its area?
questions.solution: Area of a rhombus = (product of diagonals)/2 = 16 × 12 / 2 = 96 cm².

questions.question: What is the volume of a right circular cone of base radius 7 cm and height 12 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
A wire bent into a square encloses an area of 121 cm². The same wire is bent into a circle. What is the area of the circle? (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution: Side of the square = √121 = 11 cm, so the wire is 4 × 11 = 44 cm long. As a circle, 2πr = 44 gives r = 7 cm. Area = (22/7) × 7² = 154 cm².

questions.question: A solid metal hemisphere of radius 9 cm is melted and recast into small solid spheres, each of radius 1.5 cm. How many spheres are obtained?
questions.solution: Number of spheres = volume of hemisphere / volume of one sphere = (2/3)π × 9³ ÷ [(4/3)π × 1.5³] = 486π ÷ 4.5π = 108.

questions.question: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 1440°. How many sides does it have?
questions.solution: Sum of interior angles = (n − 2) × 180°. So (n − 2) × 180 = 1440, n − 2 = 8 and n = 10.

questions.question: What is the length of the longest rod that can be placed in a room 12 m long, 9 m wide and 8 m high?
questions.solution: The longest rod lies along the room's diagonal: √(12² + 9² + 8²) = √(144 + 81 + 64) = √289 = 17 m.

questions.question: Two circles of radii 8 cm and 3 cm have their centres 13 cm apart. What is the length of a direct common tangent to the two circles?
questions.solution: Length of a direct common tangent = √(d² − (r₁ − r₂)²) = √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = √144 = 12 cm.

questions.question: A path 2 m wide runs all round the outside of a rectangular garden 30 m long and 20 m wide. What is the area of the path?
questions.solution: With the path, the outer rectangle is (30 + 4) m by (20 + 4) m = 34 m by 24 m, area 816 m². Area of path = 816 − 600 = 216 m².

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 11?
questions.solution: A number is divisible by 11 when the difference between the sums of its alternate digits is a multiple of 11. For 5918: (5 + 1) − (9 + 8) = −11, a multiple of 11. For 4825, 6173 and 7341 the differences are −7, 9 and 7. (5918 = 11 × 538.)

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their LCM is 225. What is their HCF?
questions.solution: Let the numbers be 3h and 5h, where h is the HCF (3 and 5 are co-prime). Their LCM = 15h = 225, so h = 15.

questions.question: How many integers from 1 to 300 are divisible by 3 or by 5, but not by both?
questions.solution: Multiples of 3: 100. Multiples of 5: 60. Multiples of both (i.e. of 15): 20. Divisible by exactly one = 100 + 60 − 2 × 20 = 120.

questions.question: What is the least number that must be added to 1,056 to make it exactly divisible by 23?
questions.solution: 1,056 = 23 × 45 + 21, so the remainder is 21. Adding 23 − 21 = 2 gives 1,058 = 23 × 46.

questions.question: How many even factors does 540 have?
questions.solution: 540 = 2² × 3³ × 5. An even factor must contain 2¹ or 2², so there are 2 choices for the power of 2, 4 for the power of 3 and 2 for the power of 5: 2 × 4 × 2 = 16.

questions.question: What is the largest four-digit number that is exactly divisible by each of 12, 15 and 18?
questions.solution: LCM of 12, 15 and 18 = 180. 9,999 = 180 × 55 + 99, so the largest multiple of 180 with four digits is 9,999 − 99 = 9,900.

questions.question: What is the unit digit of 3⁶⁵ × 6⁵⁹ × 7⁷¹?
questions.solution: Unit digits of powers of 3 and of 7 repeat every 4. 65 = 4 × 16 + 1, so 3⁶⁵ ends in 3. Every power of 6 ends in 6. 71 = 4 × 17 + 3, so 7⁷¹ ends like 7³ = 343, in 3. The product ends like 3 × 6 × 3 = 54, so the unit digit is 4.

questions.question: Which fraction is equal to the recurring decimal 0.363636…?
questions.solution: For a two-digit repeating block, 0.3636… = 36/99. Dividing numerator and denominator by 9 gives 4/11.

questions.question: A number leaves a remainder of 19 when divided by 36. What remainder does it leave when divided by 12?
questions.solution: The number is 36k + 19 for some whole number k. Since 36 is a multiple of 12, the remainder on division by 12 is the remainder of 19, which is 7.

questions.question: In a school, 60% of the students are boys. If 30% of the boys and 40% of the girls take part in sports, what percentage of all the students take part in sports?
questions.solution: Take 100 students: 60 boys and 40 girls. Boys in sports = 30% of 60 = 18; girls = 40% of 40 = 16. Total 34 out of 100, i.e. 34%.

questions.question: A man saves 20% of his income. His income increases by 25% and his savings increase by 50%. By what percentage does his expenditure increase?
questions.solution: Take income = 100: savings 20, expenditure 80. New income = 125 and new savings = 30, so new expenditure = 95. Increase = 15 on 80, which is 18.75%.

questions.question: If x% of 250 is equal to 20% of 400, what is x?

In an election between two candidates, 20% of the voters on the list did not vote and 500 of the votes cast were invalid. The winner got 55% of the valid votes and won by 2,000 votes. How many voters were on the list?
questions.solution: The margin is 55% − 45% = 10% of the valid votes, so valid votes = 2,000 / 0.1 = 20,000. Votes cast = 20,000 + 500 = 20,500, which is 80% of the list. List = 20,500 / 0.8 = 25,625.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word ARTICLE be arranged so that the vowels occupy only the even positions?
questions.solution: ARTICLE has 7 letters, with 3 vowels (A, I, E) and 4 consonants. There are exactly 3 even positions (2nd, 4th and 6th), so the vowels fill them in 3! = 6 ways and the consonants fill the other 4 places in 4! = 24 ways. Total = 6 × 24 = 144.

questions.question: A team of 4 is to be selected from 6 boys and 5 girls so that it has exactly 2 boys and 2 girls. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.solution: Choose 2 of the 6 boys in C(6, 2) = 15 ways and 2 of the 5 girls in C(5, 2) = 10 ways. Total = 15 × 10 = 150.

questions.question: In how many ways can 7 people sit around a round table if two particular people must not sit next to each other?
questions.solution: Without any condition, 7 people can sit round a table in (7 − 1)! = 720 ways. If the two sit together, treat them as one unit: (6 − 1)! = 120 arrangements, times 2 for their order = 240. So the arrangements with them apart = 720 − 240 = 480.

questions.question: Ten points are marked in a plane, and no three of them are in a straight line except four of them, which all lie on one line. How many triangles can be formed with vertices among these points?
questions.solution: Any 3 of the 10 points would form a triangle, C(10, 3) = 120 choices, except the triples taken from the 4 collinear points, which give no triangle: C(4, 3) = 4. Triangles = 120 − 4 = 116.

questions.question: How many four-digit even numbers have all four digits different?
questions.solution: Split on the last digit. If it is 0: the other three places can be filled in 9 × 8 × 7 = 504 ways. If it is 2, 4, 6 or 8 (4 choices): the first digit can be anything except 0 and the last digit (8 choices), then 8 and 7 choices remain, giving 4 × 8 × 8 × 7 = 1792. Total = 504 + 1792 = 2296.

questions.question: At a meeting, each of 12 people shakes hands once with every other person. How many handshakes take place?
questions.solution: Each handshake is a pair of people, so the number of handshakes = C(12, 2) = 12 × 11 / 2 = 66.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 different books be given to 3 students if a student may receive any number of books, including none?
questions.solution: Each of the 5 books can go to any of the 3 students independently, so the number of ways = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 3⁵ = 243.

questions.question: In how many different ways can the letters of the word MISSISSIPPI be arranged?
questions.solution: MISSISSIPPI has 11 letters: M once, I four times, S four times and P twice. Arrangements = 11! / (4! × 4! × 2!) = 39916800 / 1152 = 34650.

questions.question: Two cards are drawn at random, without replacement, from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. What is the probability that both are hearts?
questions.solution: Ways to pick 2 hearts = C(13, 2) = 78; ways to pick any 2 cards = C(52, 2) = 1326. Probability = 78/1326 = 1/17.

questions.question: A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
questions.solution: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4: 2 favourable outcomes out of 6. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

questions.question: What is the probability that a leap year, chosen at random, has 53 Sundays?
questions.solution: A leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks and 2 extra days. The 2 extra days are one of 7 equally likely pairs (Sunday–Monday, Monday–Tuesday, …, Saturday–Sunday), and 2 of these pairs contain a Sunday. Probability = 2/7.

questions.question: The probabilities that A and B can solve a problem are 1/3 and 1/4 respectively. If both try it independently, what is the probability that the problem gets solved?
questions.solution: The problem stays unsolved only if both fail: (1 − 1/3)(1 − 1/4) = (2/3)(3/4) = 1/2. So the probability that it is solved = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2.

questions.question: Three fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that all three show the same number?
questions.solution: There are 6³ = 216 equally likely outcomes, and 6 of them show the same number on all three dice (1-1-1 up to 6-6-6). Probability = 6/216 = 1/36.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red, 5 green and 6 blue balls. Three balls are drawn at random. What is the probability that they are of three different colours?
questions.solution: Ways to draw one ball of each colour = 4 × 5 × 6 = 120. Ways to draw any 3 of the 15 balls = C(15, 3) = 455. Probability = 120/455 = 24/91.

questions.question: The letters of the word PRIDE are arranged at random. What is the probability that the two vowels come together?
questions.solution: Total arrangements = 5! = 120. With I and E together, treat them as one unit: 4! = 24 arrangements, times 2 for their order = 48. Probability = 48/120 = 2/5.

questions.question: Two fair coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at most one head?
questions.solution: The four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT. All except HH have at most one head, so the probability = 3/4.

questions.question: A number is chosen at random from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is divisible by 4 or by 6?
questions.solution: Multiples of 4: 12. Multiples of 6: 8. Multiples of both, i.e. of 12: 4. Favourable = 12 + 8 − 4 = 16, so the probability = 16/50 = 8/25.

questions.question: By selling 33 metres of cloth, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 11 metres. What is his gain percentage?
questions.solution: Selling price of 33 m − cost price of 33 m = selling price of 11 m, so the cost price of 33 m = selling price of 22 m. Gain on the cost of 22 m is the price of 11 m: 11/22 × 100 = 50%.

questions.question: The cost price of 20 articles equals the selling price of 16 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: Let each article cost ₹1, so 20 articles cost ₹20, which is what 16 articles sell for. Profit on 16 articles = 20 − 16 = 4 on a cost of 16, i.e. 4/16 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper sells an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for ₹90 more, he would have gained 5%. What is the cost price?
questions.solution: The difference between a 5% gain and a 10% loss is 15% of the cost price, and this equals ₹90. Cost price = 90 / 0.15 = ₹600.

questions.question: A dealer cheats by 10% while buying and also by 10% while selling, using false weights. What is his overall gain percentage?
questions.solution: While buying he takes 1100 g but pays for 1000 g; while selling he gives 900 g but charges for 1000 g. So 1100 g, bought for the price of 1000 g, sells for the price of 1100/900 × 1000 g. Gain = 1100/900 − 1 = 2/9 = 22 2/9%.

questions.question: What is the fourth proportional to 4, 9 and 12?
questions.solution: If x is the fourth proportional, 4 : 9 = 12 : x, so 4x = 9 × 12 = 108 and x = 27.

questions.question: A purse contains ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5 by number. If the total value is ₹128, how many ₹2 coins are there?
questions.solution: Let the numbers be k, 3k and 5k. Value = 5k + 2 × 3k + 1 × 5k = 16k = 128, so k = 8. Number of ₹2 coins = 3 × 8 = 24.

questions.question: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. Ten years from now, the ratio will be 5 : 6. What is B's present age?
questions.solution: Let the ages be 3k and 4k. Then (3k + 10)/(4k + 10) = 5/6, so 18k + 60 = 20k + 50 and k = 5. B's present age = 4 × 5 = 20 years.

questions.question: A invests ₹20,000 for 12 months and B invests ₹30,000 for 8 months in a business. Out of a total profit of ₹18,000, what is A's share?
questions.solution: Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time: A = 20,000 × 12 = 2,40,000 and B = 30,000 × 8 = 2,40,000. The ratio is 1 : 1, so A gets half of ₹18,000 = ₹9,000.

questions.question: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. If each gets an increment of ₹4,000, the ratio becomes 4 : 5. What is A's present salary?
What is the third proportional to 16 and 36?
questions.solution: If x is the third proportional, 16 : 36 = 36 : x, so x = 36 × 36 / 16 = 1296/16 = 81.

questions.question: If (a + b) : (b + c) : (c + a) = 6 : 7 : 8 and a + b + c = 14, what is the value of c?
questions.solution: Let a + b = 6k, b + c = 7k and c + a = 8k. Adding, 2(a + b + c) = 21k, so 28 = 21k and k = 4/3. Then a + b = 8 and c = 14 − 8 = 6.

questions.question: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 4 and their expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 2. If each of them saves ₹2,000, what is A's income?
questions.solution: Let incomes be 5x and 4x and expenditures 3y and 2y. Then 5x − 3y = 2,000 and 4x − 2y = 2,000. From the second, y = 2x − 1,000; substituting, 5x − 6x + 3,000 = 2,000, so x = 1,000. A's income = 5 × 1,000 = ₹5,000.

questions.question: ₹3,240 is divided among A, B and C so that A gets 2/3 of B's share and B gets 3/4 of C's share. What is A's share?
What is the compound interest on ₹16,000 for 1½ years at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.solution: Half-yearly compounding at 10% a year means 5% per half-year for 3 half-years. Amount = 16,000 × 1.05³ = 16,000 × 1.157625 = ₹18,522. CI = 18,522 − 16,000 = ₹2,522.

questions.question: A sum of money at compound interest amounts to ₹6,050 in 2 years and to ₹6,655 in 3 years. What is the sum?
questions.solution: Interest earned in the third year = 6,655 − 6,050 = ₹605, which is the interest on ₹6,050 for one year: 605/6,050 = 10%. Then the principal = 6,050 / 1.1² = 6,050 / 1.21 = ₹5,000.

questions.question: In how many years will ₹4,000 amount to ₹5,200 at 6% per annum simple interest?
questions.solution: Interest needed = 5,200 − 4,000 = ₹1,200. Interest per year = 6% of 4,000 = ₹240. Time = 1,200 / 240 = 5 years.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹5,000 for 3 years at 10% per annum?

₹10,800 is split into two parts so that the simple interest on the first part at 8% per annum for 3 years equals the simple interest on the second part at 6% per annum for 5 years. What is the first part?
questions.solution: Interest on the first part = a × 8 × 3 / 100 = 24a/100; on the second = b × 6 × 5 / 100 = 30b/100. Equal interests give 24a = 30b, so a : b = 5 : 4. First part = 5/9 × 10,800 = ₹6,000.

questions.question: At what rate of compound interest per annum will ₹2,500 amount to ₹3,025 in 2 years?
A is 50% more efficient than B, and together they finish a piece of work in 18 days. In how many days can B alone finish it?
questions.solution: If B does 2 units a day, A does 3 units, so B does 2/5 of the combined daily work. Together they do 1/18 of the job a day, so B alone does 2/5 × 1/18 = 1/45. B alone takes 45 days.

questions.question: A and B together can do a job in 10 days, B and C in 15 days, and A and C in 12 days. In how many days can C alone do it?
A can do a piece of work in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work on alternate days, B starting on the first day. In how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution: Take the work as 36 units: A does 3 units a day and B 2 units. Each two-day cycle (B then A) completes 5 units, so 7 cycles = 14 days complete 35 units. On day 15 it is B's turn; the last 1 unit takes B half a day. Total = 14½ days.

questions.question: 10 men or 15 women can finish a job in 12 days. In how many days will 6 men and 11 women finish it?
questions.solution: 10 men do as much as 15 women, so 1 man = 1.5 women. 6 men + 11 women = 9 + 11 = 20 women. The job needs 15 × 12 = 180 woman-days, so 20 women take 180/20 = 9 days.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 10 hours, but because of a leak at the bottom it takes 12 hours to fill. In how many hours can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.solution: Rate of the leak = 1/10 − 1/12 = (6 − 5)/60 = 1/60 of the tank per hour. So the leak empties the full tank in 60 hours.

questions.question: A completes one-fourth of a piece of work in 5 days. How many days will he take to finish the whole work?
questions.solution: One-fourth takes 5 days, so the whole work (four quarters) takes 4 × 5 = 20 days.

questions.question: A alone can do a job in 6 days and B alone in 9 days. They take it on for ₹1,800 and, with the help of C, finish it in 3 days. How much should C be paid?
questions.solution: In 3 days A does 3/6 = 1/2 of the job and B does 3/9 = 1/3. C did the rest: 1 − 1/2 − 1/3 = 1/6. Payment is in proportion to the work done, so C gets 1/6 × 1,800 = ₹300.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 200 m, and both start running at the same moment. The thief runs at 10 km/h and the policeman at 12 km/h. How far will the thief have run when he is caught?
questions.solution: The policeman gains 12 − 10 = 2 km/h on the thief. To close the gap of 200 m = 0.2 km he needs 0.2/2 = 0.1 hour. In that time the thief runs 10 × 0.1 = 1 km.

questions.question: Two stations are 450 km apart. At 8 a.m. one train leaves each station and they travel towards each other at 70 km/h and 80 km/h. At what time do they meet?
questions.solution: They approach each other at 70 + 80 = 150 km/h, so they meet after 450/150 = 3 hours, at 8 a.m. + 3 hours = 11 a.m.

questions.question: Walking at 4 km/h, a man reaches his office 10 minutes late. Walking at 5 km/h, he reaches 5 minutes early. How far is his office?
questions.solution: The two times differ by 10 + 5 = 15 minutes = 1/4 hour. So d/4 − d/5 = 1/4, i.e. d/20 = 1/4, giving d = 5 km.

questions.question: A boat goes 24 km upstream and 28 km downstream in 6 hours. It goes 30 km upstream and 21 km downstream in 6.5 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution: Let the upstream speed be u and the downstream speed d. Then 24/u + 28/d = 6 and 30/u + 21/d = 6.5. Solving these two linear equations in 1/u and 1/d gives u = 6 km/h and d = 14 km/h. (Check: 4 + 2 = 6 and 5 + 1.5 = 6.5.) Speed in still water = (6 + 14)/2 = 10 km/h.
